public_rationale: SWE-Bench Pro supports the claim of substantial failure on complex tasks: its leading models resolved roughly a quarter of the public problems. It also records successful engineering work. Neither result establishes whether AI could sustain an entire engineering role under ordinary oversight. The expense claim has no defined measure or comparator, so the compound assertion cannot receive a supported or contradicted verdict.
limitations: A benchmark of individual problems does not reproduce an engineer's full responsibilities.
Success depends on the tools and instructions provided to the model.
The cost language cannot be converted fairly into an invented financial threshold.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI cannot do a software engineer's job, and it fails while costing huge amounts.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI can’t do the job of a software engineer, and it fails while also costing abominable amounts of money.

from_speaker: Generative AI can’t do the job of a software engineer
our_interpretation: The surrounding passage distinguishes generating code from an engineer's broader responsibilities. Read the claim as inability to perform a sustained engineering role reliably with ordinary workplace oversight.
Do not require flawless performance: human engineers also make mistakes.
No reporting period is specified. Use September 1–29, 2025, the latest calendar month observable before publication.
The expense description supplies no company, amount, cost category or comparison. It is a value judgment that cannot receive a separate numerical verdict.
Metric scope is null because this is not a claim about an identified company's finances.
criteria.support_condition: Representative end-to-end evaluations show contemporary systems unable to carry a sustained engineering workload at acceptable quality with ordinary oversight. The expense component additionally needs a stated cost basis and meaningful comparator.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A verified sustained deployment or representative trial demonstrates that a contemporary system performs an engineer's substantive responsibilities at acceptable quality and supervision levels.
